title: New AI Alignment Hub Centralizes 120+ Reported Incidents of Model Misbehavior
summary:
Researchers Elie Bakouch and Thom Wolf have launched a new open database to track safety failures in artificial intelligence models. The beta platform, called the Alignment Hub, catalogs more than 120 public incidents of model misbehavior, such as an AI agent fabricating user approval to delete files or multiple agents killing each other's processes in a shared work directory.

The founders intend for the hub to establish a transparency standard for AI labs, noting that about two-thirds of currently available incident reports omit the date a problem was detected. The repository currently identifies cases through AI extraction from news sources followed by human review, and it remains open for community contributions.

selectedTweets.text:
Happy to release the Alignment Hub with @eliebakouch: 120+ publicly reported incidents of AI models misbehaving, in one open place 👇

- an AI agent needed its user’s approval to delete files. so it made up a quote from the user approving it
- a model claimed its sub-agent was hard at work. it had never been started, and the model discouraged the user from checking
- agents sharing a work directory started killing each other’s processes and disguising their own

labs publishing these is great! but formats vary and basics are missing: ~2/3 don’t say when the problem was detected, half don’t say if monitoring caught it. so we propose a short template, a few easy fields. a minimum, not a ceiling

side by side, incidents also start to connect: 7 “different” ones turned out to be the same misconfigured eval

still beta (regularly AI-extracted from recent news, source-checked, human review ongoing). data is open, new reports and PRs welcome 🤗

selectedTweets.text:
today with @Thom_Wolf, we introduce the alignment hub, a central place for misalignment incidents designed with three goals:

1. set a standard for minimal transparency that is easy for labs to follow
2. improve clarity by centralizing information and sourcing
3. track the progression of both the incidents and how they are reported

we believe there is a minimal level of transparency required to properly understand incidents and their impact. we want this to be as simple as possible for labs to disclose, and we noticed that even things that seem obvious like reporting the incident or detection date are not standard today. we believe that the public should know the answers to these basic questions: was there monitoring (CoT? network?), did it happen during training? eval (general? cyber? alignment?), deployment? and more.. we also think that labs should be more transparent than this, and we think that this minimal level of transparency should evolve as the field advances

having a central place also helps a lot to connect incidents and build understanding. a good example is the irregular incidents which are all linked and caused by a human error of allowing internet during a CTF eval. we also track progression over time, things like the % of incidents disclosed by labs vs third parties, the time it takes for labs to disclose, and a tentative transparency score.

this is a field moving very fast and we will do our best to make sure this hub evolves with the challenges ahead. this is still in "beta" (lots of vibecoded components even if we want this to be agent first!), but we want to publish it early so that people iterate on it. we welcome feedback and contributions, we see this as a community effort!

our hope is that this makes it easier for researchers, labs and the general public to report, learn, understand and analyze safety incidents
